title: Cifral — Per-client proposal configuration (resolved)
description: The shape of `proposal_config` once the orchestrator has read the client's 'Proposal Config' Google Sheet and merged it over schemas/chapter-catalog.json. The sheet has three tabs — Chapters, Content, Rules — documented in docs/CLIENT-DRIVE-SETUP.md; this schema describes the RESOLVED object that travels in the shared envelope alongside `client_config`. Same split as pricing: the repo owns the catalog (structure), Drive owns the selection and the text. When a client has no `proposal_config_sheet_id`, the orchestrator resolves this object from the catalog defaults alone and everything still works.

source.description: Where the configuration came from. 'catalog_default' means the client has no Proposal Config sheet.

sheet_id.description: Drive id of the Proposal Config sheet, for traceability.

tier.description: Resolved document tier. Request override > Rules tab `default_tier` > 'B'.

chapters.description: Chapters to render, already filtered by tier + scope + client include/exclude, and already ordered. Only chapters present here get rendered.

id.description: Catalog id — also the render key ({#has_<id>}).

title.description: Resolved title in the proposal's language: client override if the Chapters tab set one, else the catalog title.

numero.description: Final chapter number as it appears in the document, computed AFTER exclusions so there are no gaps. Empty for unnumbered front matter; 'A', 'B', … for annexes.

sections.description: Resolved subsections, same shape minus nesting.

clauses.description: Boilerplate snippets from the sheet's Content tab whose `applies_when` matched this request, already filtered by language. Module 2's A5 stage attaches each to its chapter; the render core merges the body into that chapter's paragraph/bullet stream through the same parseNarrative() the LLM output goes through, so the template cannot tell them apart.

kind.description: clause -> prose merged into the chapter. exclusion/premise/obligation -> a numbered row in tabla_exclusiones / tabla_premisas / tabla_obligaciones. term -> a row in tabla_glosario.

id.description: Stable id, so a change order can cite 'premise 7'.

chapter_id.description: Catalog chapter or section id this attaches to.

title.description: Optional heading for the snippet. Rendered as a lead-in, not a Word heading.

body.description: Plain text, same convention as Module 2 output: paragraphs separated by a blank line, list items as '•  item'.

applies_when.description: Raw token list from the sheet, kept for traceability.

client.description: The sheet's `Client` tab: operational ids that used to be Notion columns. The split is deliberate — Notion says WHO the client is and whether they may send (client_id, status, send_mode, service_tier, commercial_contact_email, and the id of this sheet); this tab says what their document is made of, including which Drive folders it reads and writes. The resolving node merges these over the registry values, sheet first, so a client onboarded before this tab existed is unaffected.

proposals_folder_id.description: Drive folder the generated .docx/.pdf are written to. Overrides the registry column.

reference_docs_folder_id.description: Drive folder of approved past proposals, for Module 2 grounding. Overrides the registry column.

pricing_sheet_id.description: Rate-card sheet id. Overrides the registry column. Module 3 still reads the registry value — it does not open the Proposal Config sheet.

document_version.description: Document version for the cover, the footer and the version-control table. Defaults to '1.0'.

author.description: Author initials for the version-control table. Blank before this tab existed.

templates.description: The sheet's `Templates` tab: this client's .docx variants. A client is not one template per language — they have product lines, and a tender answers to a different document than a spare-parts quotation. Selection order is in `template` below.

variant.description: Variant key, lowercased. 'default' when the row does not name one.

match.description: Lowercased keywords; if one appears in the request text this variant is selected.

is_default.description: This is the fallback for its language.

template.description: The .docx chosen for THIS request, resolved where the sheet and the request are both in hand. Order, most specific first: an explicitly requested variant, a `match` keyword found in the request text, the language default, any row in that language, the other language, and finally the registry's template_id_en/_es. Null means nothing is configured anywhere — Module 4 then fails loudly rather than rendering an arbitrary document.

reason.description: Why this one was chosen, e.g. 'language_default' or "matched 'retrofit'". Reported in the Telegram alert: 'which template did this come out of' is the first question asked when a document looks wrong, and the finished PDF cannot answer it.

fields.description: The sheet's `Fields` tab: this client's OWN document variables, exposed to the template as {campos.<key>}. This is what makes a cover page client-specific without a deploy — an offer number from their ERP, an asset number, the legal name in their footer. The catalog owns the chapters; this owns everything around them that only this client has.

key.description: Tag name. Lowercase letters, digits and underscores only — tags are evaluated as Jexl expressions, so '-' would read as subtraction and an accent breaks the tag.

source.description: static -> the sheet's `value` column. request -> captured from the RFQ text by label, deterministically and never by a model (modules/proposal/field_capture.js): these are identifiers, and a plausible invented offer number on a customer's cover is worse than a blank. auto -> wired to something the pipeline already computed.

value.description: For `static`, the literal value. For `auto`, which computed value to use: proposal_number, date, version, tier, language, client_company, client_contact, client_email, client_phone, project_title, project_type, project_location, project_deadline.

labels.description: For `request`: the label(s) to look for, from the comma-separated capture_label cell. Matching folds case, accents and the º/° ordinal marks.

required.description: A required `request` field the sender did not supply appends `custom_fields.<key>` to missing_fields and marks the RFQ incomplete, so the run stops for review instead of shipping a cover with a hole in it.

version.description: Document version, from the `Client` tab's document_version. Defaults to '1.0'.

author.description: Author initials for the version-control table, from the `Client` tab.

rules.description: Writing rules from the sheet's Rules tab, injected verbatim into the A1/A2/A3 system prompts. Unknown keys are passed through — a client can add their own and reference them in a custom chapter.

terminology.description: Preferred wording, from Rules rows keyed 'term:<source>'. e.g. { 'cliente final': 'Cliente' }.

warnings.description: Non-fatal problems found while resolving the sheet (unknown chapter_id, unparseable applies_when, clause with no matching chapter). Surfaced in the Telegram alert so a config typo is visible without failing the proposal.
